\section{Per-system sensitivity}
\label{app:persys}

The limit Table~\ref{tab:persys} quotes for a system is that of its best
window, so a system whose coverage is wide is not penalised for the
shallowest window in it; the whole distribution, window by window, is the
per-window result the sensitivity of \S\ref{sec:pninetysel} is drawn from.

The limits span more than two orders of magnitude, so no single survey depth
describes the sample, and the frequency at which a system's best limit falls
is set by what the archive happens to hold toward it and not by any
property of the star. A limit also says nothing about whether a crossing there
could have been followed up: for \ZcNoRepSys{} of the \NSysClassA{} systems
no sensitivity would have been enough, because no block of another observing
session more than a day away covers a frequency the first one did.

\emph{The decorrelation column is measured where the delivery allows it and
imputed where it does not.} A system's best window lies in a block with no
phase record of its own for \NgNDecImpSys{} of the \NSysClassA{} systems,
against \NgNDecMeasSys{} measured, and the deepest limits are no better
served than the rest: of the \NgNDeep{} deepest, \NgNDeepMeas{} carry a
measured correction and \NgNDeepImp{} an imputed one, so the median quoted in
\S\ref{sec:pninetysel} is a mixture of the two, \NgDecMeasMedPct{} per cent
over the measured and \NgDecImpMedPct{} over the imputed. The systems whose
best limit carries more than a tenth are \NmDecBigSys.
The \RpDecNUn{} blocks whose delivery exposes no record are not a random
subset of the \SensDecorNBlkTot: of the \NbDecNUnBl{} of them that carry a
baseline, \NbDecPctTwelveUn{} per cent were taken with the 12\,m array,
against \NbDecPctTwelveMeas{} per cent of the blocks that do expose a record,
and it is that array's long baselines that lose coherence. Within each array
the two sets are not distinguishable -- \NbDecBlSevenUn{} against
\NbDecBlSevenMeas\,m in the median on the compact array and
\NbDecBlTwelveUn{} against \NbDecBlTwelveMeas\,m on the 12\,m one -- so the
archive withholds a configuration rather than a baseline. Matching
each of their windows to the measured blocks within a factor of two in
baseline length puts the correction at \RpDecMatchMed{} per cent in the
median, rising to \RpDecMatchHi{} per cent were their coherence as poor as
the ninetieth percentile of the blocks matched to them, so those limits are
conditional on a calibration performance the archive does not report.

\emph{The injected set is drawn by block, and that cost is measured.}
It spans both delivered response forms, \TfInjNat{} windows at the native
channelisation and \TfInjAvg{} with channels averaged online, and splitting it
there moves the ninety per cent point by \TfFacShift\,$P_{\rm trig}$. The
draw controlled the array, but the achieved mix still departs from the
population by \SensCovWorstPct{} per cent of the sample; re-weighting the
pooled curve by the survey's own composition gives
$\SensPooledArrWeighted\,P_{\rm trig}$ against the adopted
$\EirpNinetyMultA$. Because a system's limit is its best window, a minimum
over several estimates could favour windows whose own factor falls below the
class average; drawing each window's factor from the \SensNInj{} measured
ones instead, over \ScRsNTrial{} trials, leaves the per-system median where
it is -- the shift is \ScRsMedShiftPct{} per cent -- and holds the count at
$10^{15}$\,W to \ScRsNLo--\ScRsNHi{} in nine trials in ten.

$\epsilon$~Eri's window also omits the annual parallax and is optimistic by
at most \BmEpsPxBoundPct{} per cent on that account
(Appendix~\ref{app:pbresp}).
The last column records whether two execution blocks of different observing

lower bounds, since two blocks can be shown to be separated but never shown
to be simultaneous.
